sentiment_reasoning: Triple headwind: Iran-Israel missile exchange reignites Strait of Hormuz fears sending Brent above $97, semiconductor sell-off from Broadcom's AI guidance miss erased $1T and triggered KOSPI circuit breakers, and a blowout May jobs report (172K vs 85K) shifts Fed pricing toward a December rate hike. All three forces compound — energy inflation feeds into hot CPI due Tuesday, rate hike fears crush growth multiples, and geopolitical risk squeezes margins for energy-importing sectors.

summary.gist: Markets face a three-front assault this Monday: fresh Iran-Israel missile exchanges over the weekend have sent Brent crude surging 5% above $97 and threaten further Strait of Hormuz disruption; the Broadcom-led semiconductor rout ($1T destroyed, KOSPI circuit breaker triggered) signals AI euphoria is cracking; and Friday's blowout May payrolls report (172K vs 85K expected) has pushed December rate hike odds to 70%, crushing rate-sensitive growth names. The dominant force is energy-driven stagflation risk — oil above $95 with a hawkish Fed is the worst possible cocktail for equities.

executive_summary: Monday opens under severe pressure as Iran and Israel exchanged missile strikes over the weekend, sending Brent crude surging 4.9% to $97.68 and reigniting fears of further Strait of Hormuz disruption. This compounds last week's semiconductor carnage — Broadcom's underwhelming AI chip guidance triggered a $1 trillion sell-off across the chip supply chain, with the Nasdaq losing 4.2% on its worst day since April 2025 and South Korea's KOSPI hitting circuit breakers Monday morning at -8.4%. The third blow comes from Friday's unexpectedly strong May jobs report (172K vs 85K expected), which has pushed Fed rate hike odds for December to 70% and sent the 10-year yield to 4.55%. With May CPI due Tuesday and the first FOMC meeting under new Chair Kevin Warsh on June 16-17, markets face a gauntlet of catalysts that all point toward tighter financial conditions and compressed equity multiples.

macro_events.title: Iran-Israel Missile Exchange Reignites Hormuz Crisis
macro_events.causal_chain: Iran IRGC launched Operation Nasr targeting two Israeli military bases June 7 → Israel retaliated with strikes on central/western Iran June 8 → Strait of Hormuz blocked since February 2026 air war → 21% of global traded oil + 20% of LNG transits Hormuz → war-risk insurance premiums spike on VLCCs → Brent +4.9% to $97.68, WTI +3.4% to $93.63 → Asian refiners reroute via Cape of Good Hope (+12-14 days, +$2M/trip) → tanker rates surge → energy cost pass-through hits consumer prices → CPI risk tilts higher ahead of Tuesday print
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East → Global energy → Asian refiners → European gas (Dutch TTF) → US inflation
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack: Brent +15% in 24h, tankers ran 20-35% in one week. Current crisis more severe given prolonged Hormuz closure since February.
macro_events.counterargument: April 8 ceasefire held for two months; both sides may pull back. US SPR releases and OPEC+ spare capacity could cap oil above $100.

macro_events.title: Broadcom AI Guidance Miss Triggers $1T Semiconductor Rout
macro_events.causal_chain: Broadcom Q3 AI chip guidance $16B missed $17.2B consensus → did not raise FY2026 AI forecast → sell-the-news cascade → AVGO -14%, Nasdaq -4.18% worst since Apr 2025 → SOX -10%, $1T erased in two sessions → Asia contagion: Samsung -10%, SK Hynix -10%, KOSPI circuit breaker at -8.37% → memory chip crisis deepens → multiple compression across AI-adjacent names
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US → South Korea (circuit breaker) → Japan (Nikkei -4.2%) → Taiwan (-3.9%) → Global chip supply chain
macro_events.historical_analog: Cisco Jan 2001: guidance miss after internet capex buildup triggered 40% sector de-rating over 6 months.
macro_events.counterargument: NVDA showed resilience at -6% vs peers -10-17%. Google $920M/month GPU deal confirms hyperscaler demand. May be healthy rotation not cycle peak.

macro_events.title: Blowout May Jobs Report Shifts Fed Toward Rate Hike
macro_events.causal_chain: May NFP 172K crushed 85K consensus → unemployment steady 4.3% → markets reprice Dec rate hike from 50% to 70% → 10Y at 4.55%, 30Y at 5.01% → DXY strengthens to 100.11 → higher discount rates crush growth valuations → strong labor + $97 oil = stagflation risk → gold drops to $4,337 (2026 low) as real rates rise
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US labor → Treasury curve → Global FX → EM currency stress
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2023: Hot jobs sent 10Y to 4.8%, triggered 5% SPX correction over 3 weeks.
macro_events.counterargument: One strong print doesn't make trend; April was soft at 65K. New Chair Warsh may prioritize growth. Services inflation may be peaking.

macro_events.title: May CPI Report Due Tuesday — Energy Inflation Risk
macro_events.causal_chain: April CPI +0.6% MoM, 3.8% YoY with energy +3.8% driving 40%+ → May data June 10 → Brent averaged $92-95 through May with Hormuz disruption → energy component elevated → hot print validates rate hike pricing → FOMC June 16-17 becomes live for hawkish guidance
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US consumer prices → Fed policy → Global risk appetite
macro_events.counterargument: Core ex-energy may moderate. Used car deflation could offset. Market may have priced in hot number.
